brief.headline: Match Shrinath Roto Pack's ₹290.00/KG price for laminates and push payment terms from 30 to 53 days to free up ₹18.97 L in cash — they're losing money and carry high debt, so lead with supply security and a backup plan.

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match ₹290.00/KG across all laminate SKUs
priceAsk.target: ₹290.00/KG (the price Shrinath Roto Pack gives us); this saves ₹3.91 L per year
priceAsk.basis: We already pay ₹290.00/KG to Shrinath Roto Pack for the same laminates. GLS charges us ₹295.00/KG — a 1.7% gap. The market asking price band is ₹205–305/kg with ₹250/kg typical, so their ₹295 sits at the top of fair; ₹290 is well inside it and proven by our own books.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Push payment terms from 30 days to 53 days (matching how long they take to pay their own suppliers)
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Extending to 53 days frees up ₹18.97 L in cash for us; even a move to 45 days (15 days more) frees up ₹9.49 L

brief.financialLeverage: GLS made a loss in FY2024-25 (₹-23.68 Cr) and keeps -3.4% of every ₹100 they sell, well behind similar firms at 2.5%. They owe 2.15 times their own cash (₹208.21 Cr total debt) and borrow money at about 10.96%, so cash is tight for them. Their Altman Z-score is 1.68 (grey zone — neither healthy nor in distress, but watch carefully). Our ₹2.31 Cr annual spend is only 0.33% of their ₹691.05 Cr revenue, so we're small to them — don't have much volume muscle, but their weak position means they need stable customers. Push on payment terms and price benchmarking, but don't squeeze so hard you tip a fragile supplier; keep a backup ready.

evidence.figure: ₹-23.68 Cr final profit in FY2024-25; -3.4% kept vs 2.5% for similar firms

evidence.point: They owe a lot and pay high interest

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter already supplying FDC in small volumes — proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets; ₹2755.75 Cr revenue, C (58/100) health

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant doing both film substrate and conversion — can second-source laminates at scale; ₹17547.92 Cr revenue, C (48/100) health

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter specializing in pharma blister and sachet laminates — strong fit for our ORS sachets; ₹222.04 Cr revenue, D (31/100) health

risks: They lost ₹23.68 Cr in FY2024-25 and sit in the grey zone (Altman Z 1.68) — pushing too hard on price could tip them over and strand our supply; lead with payment terms and volume stability, not just price cuts
Credit rating is IVR BBB- / Stable and overall health D (21/100) with a 2/10 money-health score — don't concentrate too much volume here; qualify a second source now
Multiple red flags on file: severe legal case(s), GST filing delays, EPF payment delays, high leverage — sign of operational stress; shorten lead times and monitor delivery closely
We're only 0.33% of their ₹691.05 Cr revenue — limited volume leverage; the ask must lean on fairness (matching our best price, matching their own payment cycle) rather than threatening to walk
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're paying ₹295 when Shrinath gives us ₹290 for the same laminates — let's close that ₹5 gap and talk about extending payment terms to 53 days, which matches how you pay your own suppliers.
